items.title: A proposed order authorizing the Corporation Counsel to enter into and execute a Settlement Order in the following sixteen (16) cases

enrichment.relevance_reason: This item is a settlement of sixteen lawsuits against police officers, such as Guevara, with no connection to building, financing, regulating, or taxing homes or tenants' rights.

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of an intergovernmental agreement with the Chicago Board of Education to provide TIF funds for improvements at Harriet Beecher Stowe Elementary School, located at 3444 W. Wabansia Avenue.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item provides TIF funds for improvements to an elementary school, which does not involve building, financing, preserving, regulating, taxing, or demolishing homes or the rights of residents.

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of an intergovernmental agreement with the Chicago Board of Education to provide TIF funds for improvements at Suder Montessori Magnet Elementary School, located at 2022 W. Washington Boulevard.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item provides TIF funds for capital improvements at an elementary school, which is an institutional use with no dwelling units or residential regulation involved.

items.title: A substitute ordinance approving the execution of the 66th amending agreement with SomerCor 504, Inc. to increase the amount of grant funds available in various redevelopment project areas, amend the Small Business Improvement Fund (SBIF) program rules, and authorize SomerCor 504, Inc. to continue providing administrative services for the program.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item concerns grant funds and administrative services for the Small Business Improvement Fund, which assists small businesses rather than building, financing, preserving, or regulating homes or residents' rights.

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of a Redevelopment Agreement with BTH Development, NFP to provide Housing and Economic Development Bond (HED) funds for redevelopment of Altgeld Gardens Youth Center project at 13122 S. Ellis Avenue.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item funds redevelopment of a youth center, a community facility, and the material does not mention any housing units.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance authorizing a Redevelopment Agreement with BTH Development, NFP to provide up to $7,300,000 in Housing and Economic Development Bond funds for redevelopment of the Altgeld Gardens Youth Center at 13122 S. Ellis Avenue (10th Ward).

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of a Redevelopment Agreement with North Lawndale Catalyst Initiative, NFP to provide Housing and Economic Development (HED) funds and tax increment financing (TIF) assistance for the Filmore Linen Services project at 920-922 S. Campbell Avenue.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item funds a linen services project, which appears to be commercial or economic development, and the material mentions no homes.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance authorizing a Redevelopment Agreement with North Lawndale Catalyst Initiative, NFP for up to $5,000,000 in HED funds and up to $5,000,000 in TIF assistance for the Filmore Linen Services project at 920-922 S. Campbell Avenue (28th Ward).

items.title: An ordinance authorizing the execution of a Redevelopment Agreement with Hudson Michigan Avenue Owner LLC to provide Housing and Economic Development (HED) funds for the Hudson House project at 2222 S. Michigan Avenue.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance would provide city HED loan and grant funds to a redevelopment project called Hudson House, which appears to be a housing project, though the material does not describe its use.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance authorizing a Redevelopment Agreement with Hudson Michigan Avenue Owner LLC for the Hudson House project at 2222 S. Michigan Avenue in the 3rd Ward. It provides up to $5,000,000 in HED city loan funds and up to $10,000,000 in HED city grant funds.

items.title: One (1) proposed order authorizing the payment of various small claims against the City of Chicago.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item is a routine order authorizing payment of small claims against the City, which does not bear on homes, housing finance, or tenants' rights.

items.title: One (1) proposed orders denying the payment of various small claims against the City of Chicago.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item denies payment of various small claims against the City, which is a routine claims-settlement matter with no bearing on building, financing, regulating, or taxing homes or tenants' rights.

items.title: Appointment of Vernell Givens as Commissioner of Chicago Housing Authority for a term effective immediately and expiring August 31, 2031.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item is an appointment of a Chicago Housing Authority commissioner, which bears on governance of public housing in Chicago.
enrichment.summary: The City Council Committee on Housing and Real Estate will consider the appointment of Vernell Givens as a Chicago Housing Authority Commissioner, with a term effective immediately and expiring August 31, 2031.

items.title: Appointment of Mary Gardner as Commissioner of Chicago Housing Authority for a term effective immediately and expiring August 31, 2031.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item concerns an appointment to the Chicago Housing Authority board, the agency that runs public housing in Chicago.
enrichment.summary: The Committee on Housing and Real Estate will consider the appointment of Mary Gardner as a Commissioner of the Chicago Housing Authority, with a term effective immediately and expiring August 31, 2031.

items.title: Appointment of Hipolito (Paul) Roldan as Commissioner of Chicago Housing Authority

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item is a mayoral appointment of a Chicago Housing Authority commissioner, which bears on the governance of public housing.
enrichment.summary: Mayor Brandon Johnson has appointed Hipolito (Paul) Roldan as a Chicago Housing Authority commissioner for a term effective immediately and expiring July 7, 2031. The appointment goes to the City Council for consideration.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 11414 S Halsted St to Far South CDC under Low-Income Housing Tax Credits program for redevelopment of Morgan Park Commons (repeal and replacement of O2026-0026567 in entirety)

attachments.label: O2026-0029008 Ex C Site Plan and Project Phases
O2026-0029008 Ex B Legal Description of Dev Property

enrichment.relevance_reason: It authorizes sale of City-owned land for $1 to a nonprofit developer for a mixed-income, affordable housing redevelopment tied to Low-Income Housing Tax Credits and the ARO.
enrichment.summary: Repeals and replaces ordinance O2026-0026567, authorizing sale of City-owned property at 11414 S Halsted St to Far South CDC for $1 for Morgan Park Commons. Phase 1 would build two mixed-income buildings with 70 units, 66 affordable; Phase 0 is site work funded by a $15 million state grant.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 1335 S Springfield Ave to MKB Business Strategies LLC in Trust for Use of Schools

attachments.label: O2026-0029007 Ex B Depiction of Property

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance sells a surplus school site to a developer that plans to demolish the building and build affordable single-family homes and three-flats.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance would convey the former Henson Elementary campus parcel at 1335 S Springfield Ave to MKB Business Strategies, LLC for $25,000. MKB plans to demolish the building and build 13 single-family houses and 13 affordable three-flats in two phases.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 2830 W Wilcox St, 2860 W Cermak Rd, 5016 S Christiana Ave, 7713 S Dobson St, 5008, 5010, 5012, 5014, 5016 and 5018 S Throop St to various buyers under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance sells vacant City-owned lots to buyers for community open space under a deed restriction requiring open space improvements, not for building, preserving, or regulating homes.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 1948 W 63rd St to Reynoso Insulation LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The sale of two vacant city-owned lots is for a commercial parking lot serving an adjacent business, with no housing units involved.
enrichment.summary: The ordinance would sell two vacant City-owned lots at 1948 W 63rd St for $18,006 to Reynoso Insulation, LLC through ChiBlockBuilder. The buyer plans a commercial parking lot for its adjacent business, with no ARO units.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 2054 and 2058 W Warren Blvd to EGP Warren Apartments LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance sells City-owned vacant land for a 20-unit residential building that includes four ARO-compliant affordable units.
enrichment.summary: The City Council would approve the sale of two City-owned parcels at 2054 and 2058 W. Warren Blvd to EGP Warren Apartments LLC for $315,315 through ChiBlockBuilder. The buyer would build a 20-unit residential building including four ARO-compliant units.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 4927, 4935 and 4937 S Forrestville Ave to TK Palos LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance sells city-owned vacant lots for construction of 16 residential units in Grand Boulevard, with ARO units required, and disposes of public land for housing.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance would sell three city-owned parcels at 4927, 4935 and 4937 S Forrestville Ave to TK Palos LLC for $301,028 through ChiBlockBuilder. The buyer would build two 8-unit masonry residential buildings; the project will contain ARO units.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 4549 S Indiana Ave to Click Development LLC 4549 Indiana under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance sells a vacant City-owned lot for construction of a new 16-unit residential building that includes two ARO units.
enrichment.summary: City Council would approve sale of City-owned vacant land at 4549 S. Indiana Ave. to Click Development, LLC 4549 Indiana for $203,241 through ChiBlockBuilder. The buyer would build a 16-unit residential building, including two ARO units, with a deed restriction.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 3729, 3731 and 3733 S Giles Ave to Iron Eagle LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: It is a sale of three City-owned residential lots for construction of new multi-unit housing under the ChiBlockBuilder program.
enrichment.summary: The City would sell three vacant lots at 3729, 3731 and 3733 S Giles Ave in Douglas to Iron Eagle LLC for $250,000 under ChiBlockBuilder. The buyer would build three three-story buildings with three 3-bedroom units each, with no ARO units.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 1509 E 67th Pl to 1509 E. 67th PL LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: It approves the sale of a vacant City-owned lot for market-rate development through the ChiBlockBuilder program, which is disposition of public land for housing.
enrichment.summary: The City Council would approve sale of vacant City-owned land at 1509 E. 67th Pl to 1509 E. 67th PL LLC for market-rate development, via the Department of Planning and Development's ChiBlockBuilder program, subject to a deed restriction and closing conditions.

items.title: Sale of City-owned property at 4849, 4853 and 4857 W West End Ave to Medlock Development LLC under ChiBlockBuilder

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance would sell vacant City-owned land for a 15-unit new-construction residential project, a disposition of public land for housing.
enrichment.summary: The City Council would approve the as-is sale of City-owned lots at 4849, 4853 and 4857 W West End Ave to Medlock Development LLC through ChiBlockBuilder, for market-rate development. The disclosure describes a 15-unit new construction project.

items.title: President’s Update

enrichment.relevance_reason: The CLIHTF board oversees Chicago's Low-Income Housing Trust Fund, which subsidizes rental housing for low-income tenants, though this item is only a general president's update.
enrichment.summary: The President's Update is a standing item on the CLIHTF Board of Directors' October 13, 2026 agenda. The material gives no details of its content.

items.title: Reports

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund board hears committee reports on rental subsidy allocations, a property ownership change, and a draft 2027 budget for its affordable rental subsidy program.
enrichment.summary: CLIHTF board receives committee reports, including an allocations summary, an ownership change of 6815 N Sheridan from Patricia Johnson to Teko Properties, financial statements through September 30, 2026, and the draft 2027 budget.

items.title: Allocations Summary

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund board is receiving its Allocations Committee report on rental subsidy allocations for low-income housing.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board of Directors will receive an Allocations Summary from the Allocations Committee, chaired by Adonya Little. No allocation amounts, properties, or unit counts are given beyond the agenda title.

items.title: Ownership change of 6815 N Sheridan from Patricia Johnson to Teko Properties

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item concerns an ownership change for a rental property at 6815 N Sheridan, which is handled through the Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund's rental subsidy program.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board's Allocations Committee report includes an ownership change for 6815 N Sheridan from Patricia Johnson to Teko Properties. The material gives no further details.

items.title: Financial Statements as of September 30, 2026

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund, which funds rental subsidies for low-income tenants, will review its financial statements as part of its board's oversight of affordable housing funding.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board's Finance and Audit Committee, with Treasurer Meredith Muir, will report on the Trust Fund's financial statements as of September 30, 2026. The same meeting includes a draft 2027 budget presentation.

items.title: Presentation of draft 2027 Budget

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund's 2027 budget governs funding for its rental subsidy program for low-income renters.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board's Finance and Audit Committee, with Treasurer Meredith Muir reporting, will present a draft 2027 budget for the Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund. No budget figures are provided in the material.

items.title: Outreach Committee Update provided by Board VP Sam Paler-Ponce

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund board is receiving an update on its outreach work, which supports its rental subsidy program for low-income tenants.
enrichment.summary: Board Vice President Sam Paler-Ponce will give an Outreach Committee update at the CLIHTF Board of Directors meeting. The agenda gives no further detail on the update.

items.title: New Business: Tenant Outreach Initiative presented by Marlana Edwards, Director of Program Development and Outreach

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund board will hear a Tenant Outreach Initiative, which concerns tenants in subsidized rental housing.
enrichment.summary: The CLIHTF Board of Directors will hear a new-business presentation on a Tenant Outreach Initiative from Marlana Edwards, Director of Program Development and Outreach. The material gives no further detail on the initiative.

items.title: Establishment of Problem Landlord and Housing Court Coordination Task Force to examine and recommend improvements to response to chronic and repeat housing code violations

enrichment.relevance_reason: The resolution creates a task force on enforcing building codes against problem landlords and coordinating with housing and eviction court, which bears on habitability and tenant protections.
enrichment.summary: A City Council resolution would create a Problem Landlord and Housing Court Coordination Task Force. It would include aldermen, Mayor's Office, Buildings, Law and Circuit Court representatives. The task force would recommend improvements on repeat building code violations and report within 180 days of its first meeting.

items.title: Amendment of Municipal Code Section 17-9-0129 allowing lawful cannabis dispensaries to modify to include medical cannabis without triggering Section 17-9-0129.1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance regulates cannabis dispensary operations and permitting under the zoning code without changing rules for dwelling units or residential use, so it does not bear on homes.

items.title: Amendment of Municipal Code Chapter 17-3 by adding Section 17-3-0600 regarding transient-oriented development (TOD) streets

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance amends the Zoning Ordinance to set TOD street rezoning requirements (B or C1 districts with minimum 3 FAR) and lowers the residential parking cap near transit, affecting where and how housing can be built.
enrichment.summary: Proposed ordinance adds Section 17-3-0600 creating TOD streets near CTA/Metra stations, requiring rezonings there to B or C1 districts with at least 3 FAR and setting design standards. It also lowers the residential parking cap near transit to 0.5 spaces per unit.

items.title: Designation of segment of N Western Ave right-of-way on Map Nos. 9-H, 9-I, 11-H, 11-I, 13-H, and 13-I as Transient Oriented Development (TOD) Street and amendment of Municipal Code Section 17-3-0602-F designating portion of N Western Ave as Transient Oriented Development (TOD) Street

attachments.label: TOD Street - Western Avenue - Addison to Ainslie (1)

enrichment.relevance_reason: Designating a TOD street in the Chicago Zoning Ordinance changes zoning rules that govern residential density and parking for development along N Western Ave.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance would designate N Western Avenue between W Addison St and W Ainslie St as a Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Street and amend Municipal Code Section 17-3-0602-F accordingly. Sponsored by Aldermen Matthew J. Martin (47th) and Andre Vasquez Jr. (40th).

items.title: Designation of segment of N Ravenswood Ave right-of-way on Map No. 11-H as Transient Oriented Development (TOD) Street and amendment of Municipal Code Section 17-3-0602-F designating portion of N Ravenswood Ave as Transient Oriented Development Street

attachments.label: TOD Street -  Ravenswood Avenue - Irving Park to Lawrence

enrichment.relevance_reason: TOD street designation changes zoning rules (such as parking and density allowances) for residential and mixed-use development along a corridor, affecting housing supply.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance sponsored by Alderman Matthew J. Martin (47th Ward) would designate N Ravenswood Ave between W Irving Park Rd and W Lawrence Ave as a Transit Oriented Development street, amending Municipal Code Section 17-3-0602-F and Map No. 11-H.

items.title: Repeal of historical landmark designation for Cortland Bridge

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance repeals a historical landmark designation for a bridge, which concerns no homes, dwelling units, or residential rights.

items.title: Historical landmark fee waiver for property at 208 S LaSalle St

attachments.label: Permit Fee Waiver - 208 S LaSalle signed

enrichment.relevance_reason: The order waives city permit fees for converting floors of a historic downtown building into 167 residential units, 30% of them affordable at 60% AMI.
enrichment.summary: An order from Ald. Brendan Reilly would waive city permit fees from 10/01/2026 through 7/01/2028 for adaptive reuse of floors 14-16 at 208 S. LaSalle St. into 167 dwelling units, 30% affordable at 60% AMI. Owner is 208 LaSalle Owner, LLC.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map Nos. 1-H and 3-H at 1600-1760 W Chicago Ave and 1601-1759 W Chicago Ave

enrichment.relevance_reason: A corridor-wide rezoning from B1 neighborhood shopping to B3 community shopping districts changes the zoning rules that govern what, including residential, can be built along West Chicago Avenue.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance sponsored by Alderman Daniel La Spata (1st Ward) would rezone B1-2 and B1-3 parcels along W Chicago Ave between N Wood St and N Ashland Ave to B3-2 and B3-3. Several parcels with other zoning are excluded.

geography.address: 1600-1760 W. Chicago Ave and 1601-1759 W. Chicago Ave

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 10-F at 4639-4643 S Wallace St

enrichment.relevance_reason: A residential downzoning from B2-3 mixed-use to RS-3 single-unit detached house district changes the housing that can be built on the site.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance sponsored by Ald. Raymond A. Lopez (15th Ward) would rezone 4639-43 S Wallace Street on Map No. 10-F from B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District to RS-3 Residential Single Unit (Detached House) District.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 12-F at 5000-5046 S Wells St

enrichment.relevance_reason: The ordinance rezones land from a neighborhood shopping district to a single-unit residential district, changing what housing can be built on the site.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance would rezone the area bounded by West 50th Street, South Wells Street, and the alley to the west, at 5000-5046 S Wells St, from B1-1 Neighborhood Shopping District to RS-3 Residential Single-Unit (Detached House) District. Sponsored by Alderwoman Jeanette B. Taylor, 20th Ward.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 17-H at 1721 W Greenleaf Ave

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning changes a residential RT-4 two-flat/townhouse/multi-unit district to a B3-3 Community Shopping District, which affects land currently zoned for housing.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance sponsored by Ald. Maria Hadden (49th Ward) would rezone the area at 1721 W. Greenleaf Ave from RT-4 Residential Two-Flat, Townhouse and Multi-Unit District to B3-3 Community Shopping District. It also includes necessary relief under Sections 17-13-1003 and 17-13-1101.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map Nos. 8-F and 10-F at 3800-3958 S State St, 3901-3959 S Dearborn St, 3900-3958 S Dearborn St, 3901-3959 S Federal St, 3900-3946 S Federal St, 2-24 W Pershing Rd, 1-109 W Pershing Rd and 2-52 W 40th St - App No. 23087

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning amends Business Planned Development No. 1143 to expand its boundaries onto RS-3 and RT-4 land and City-owned parcels for a phased mixed-use project that includes multi-family housing and is subject to the ARO.
enrichment.summary: P.S. Bronzeville, LLC seeks to rezone RS-3, RT-4 and PD 1143 land near 39th and State to an expanded Business Planned Development No. 1143. Phase I is a grocery-anchored mixed-use development; Phase II, north of Pershing, would include multi-family housing. The application checks that the project is subject to the ARO.

geography.address: 3800-3958 S State St, 3901-3959 S Dearborn St, 3900-3958 S Dearborn St, 3901-3959 S Federal St, 3900-3946 S Federal St, 2-24 W Pershing Rd, 1-109 W Pershing Rd and 2-52 W 40th St

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No.  4-E at 1608 S Wabash Ave - App No. 23131

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from DX-5 to DS-3 at 1608 S. Wabash is for a storage and delivery use of construction materials with zero dwelling units and no residential use proposed, so it is a purely commercial/industrial map amendment that does not add, remove, or change homes.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 10-E at 3927-3933 S Martin Luther King, Jr. Dr. - App No. 23135

enrichment.relevance_reason: The item rezones a vacant lot from RM-5 to B3-3 for a restaurant building with zero dwelling units and no residential use proposed, so it is a purely commercial rezoning that does not add, remove, or change homes.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 12-K at 5312 S Kenneth Ave - App No. 23172

enrichment.relevance_reason: A rezoning of a residential lot with an existing multi-unit building from RS-2 to RT-4 affects the legal residential density and compliance of existing homes.
enrichment.summary: Midway 5312 S. Kenneth Avenue Condominium seeks to rezone 5312 S. Kenneth Ave from RS-2 to RT-4 to unify the lot under one zoning designation and bring a building built contrary to approved plans into compliance. The use stays residential with 3 dwelling units.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 3-I at 1140 N California Ave - App No. 23162T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from B3-1 to B3-3 would allow a commercial/medical behavioral health clinic on a vacant lot, with no dwelling units involved.
enrichment.summary: Humboldt Park Health seeks to rezone 1140 N. California Ave. from B3-1 to B3-3 Community Shopping District to build a 3-story outpatient behavioral health clinic, urgent care center and medical office, with a 100% parking reduction sought.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 13-L at 4841 N Lipps Ave- App No. 23163

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning would permit renovation of an existing mixed-use building to contain four dwelling units above a ground-floor commercial space.
enrichment.summary: 4841 Lipps LLC seeks to rezone 4841 N. Lipps Ave. from B3-2 to C1-2 to renovate an existing mixed-use building into one ground-floor commercial space and four dwelling units. Ald. Gardiner has stated no objection.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 12-D at 5482 S Ridgewood Ct - App No. 23170T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A residential rezoning from RT-4 to RM-4.5 changes the zoning district for a home, with setback and open-space variations for a rear addition to an existing single-family house.
enrichment.summary: Rezones 5482 S Ridgewood Ct from RT-4 to RM-4.5 so homeowners Nabil M. Abou Baker and Sara G. Jelinek can replace the home's rear addition, with setback and rear yard open space relief. No parking is provided and no new units are proposed.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 2-K at 4125 and 4127 W 5th Ave - App No. 23171T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A Type 1 rezoning from RT-4 to RM-4.5 on city-owned vacant lots would allow two new three-unit residential buildings.
enrichment.summary: TechCo Savvy Inc. seeks to rezone city-owned vacant lots at 4125 and 4127 W 5th Ave from RT-4 to RM-4.5 to build two three-story buildings with three units each. It is working with the Department of Housing to acquire the lots, and also requests setback variations.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 4-H at 2142 W 18th Pl - App No. 23173T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A residential rezoning from RT-4 to RM-5 that legalizes an existing five-unit building and splits off a vacant lot for a new three-unit building.
enrichment.summary: Coach House Properties LLC seeks to rezone 2142 W 18th Pl from RT-4 to RM-5 to split two lots. The change would legalize the existing five-unit building, while the vacant lot stays RT-4 for a new three-unit building.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 7-H at 2315-2317 W Barry Ave - App No. 23169T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A residential rezoning from RS-3 to RT-4 would allow renovation and expansion of an existing three-unit residential building.
enrichment.summary: Ordinance would rezone 2315-17 W Barry Ave from RS-3 to RT-4 so the applicant can renovate and add a rear addition to an existing three-unit building. The plans list ZSD Barry LLC as developer/owner; the unit count stays at three.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 5-H at 1933 N Winchester Ave - App No. 23175T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: A residential rezoning that would legalize an existing fifth dwelling unit in a building now zoned for fewer units.
enrichment.summary: Theus Property Holding - 1933 N. Winchester L.L.C. seeks to rezone 1933 N Winchester Ave from RS-3 to RM-4.5 so the existing fifth unit and rooftop dormer conform. No expansion is proposed; the building stays at five units and 29 feet.
entities: Theus Property Holding - 1933 N. Winchester L.L.C.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 15-J at 3244-3250 W Bryn Mawr Ave - App No. 23176T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Type 1 map amendment application would allow a mixed-use building with 40 residential units on a vacant commercial site and is subject to the ARO.
enrichment.summary: 3244-50 Bryn Mawr LLC seeks to amend a previously approved Type 1 map amendment (B2-3 to B2-3) at 3244-50 W Bryn Mawr Ave. It would allow a five-story building with 40 residential units, 1,490 sq. ft. of ground-floor commercial space and 25 parking spaces. The application says the project is subject to the ARO.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 18-E at 7353-7359 S Indiana Ave - App No. 23148T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from RS2 to RT4 would allow a new 8-unit residential building on a vacant lot.
enrichment.summary: 73RD AND INDIANA, LLC seeks to rezone 7353-59 S Indiana Ave from RS2 to RT4 to build a two-story, 8-unit residential building with a 7-car garage on a vacant lot. The application says the ARO does not apply.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 1-H at 2156 W Warren Blvd - App No. 23147T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from RT4 to RM5 would allow a new 8-unit residential building on a vacant lot.
enrichment.summary: 2156 W Warren LLC seeks to rezone a vacant lot at 2156 W Warren Blvd from RT4 to RM5 to build a 4-story, 8-unit residential building with 5 outdoor parking spaces. The application says the project is not subject to the ARO.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 2-I at 2400 W Grenshaw St a.k.a. 1124 S Western Ave - App No. 23149T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from C1-2 to B2-3 would allow a new 7-unit residential building, including ground-floor residential use, on a vacant lot.
enrichment.summary: Applicant seeks a Type 1 rezoning of 2400 W. Grenshaw St. from C1-2 Neighborhood Commercial to B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use, with a rear setback variation, to build a 4-story, 7-unit residential building with 3 garage parking spaces on a vacant corner lot.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 8-G at 3439 S Morgan St - App No. 23152T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning would allow a new six-unit residential building on a vacant lot, with reduced parking under the transit-served location provisions.
enrichment.summary: QHN LLC seeks to rezone 3439 S Morgan St from B1-3 to B2-3 to build a three-story, six-unit residential building on a vacant lot. It also requests a parking reduction from six spaces to three under the Transit Served Location rules. The project is not subject to the ARO.

items.title: Zoning Reclassification Map No. 1-H at 1921 W Chicago Ave - App No. 23153T1

enrichment.relevance_reason: The rezoning from B3-2 to B3-3 would allow a new four-story mixed-use building with three residential units replacing a two-story residence.

enrichment.relevance_reason: The hearing covers IHDA's proposed issuance of up to $500 million in mortgage revenue bonds to finance home mortgage loans and down payment assistance in Illinois.
enrichment.summary: IHDA will hold a TEFRA public hearing on October 15, 2026 on issuing up to $500,000,000 in mortgage revenue bonds (2026 Series LMNO) over three years. Proceeds would finance qualifying mortgage loans, down payment and closing cost assistance, and refund prior bonds.

notices.title: Public Notice on IHDA’s Draft 2027-2028 Qualified Allocation Plan – English – Spanish

enrichment.relevance_reason: The Qualified Allocation Plan sets how Illinois awards Low-Income Housing Tax Credits for affordable housing development.
enrichment.summary: IHDA released its draft 2027-2028 Low-Income Housing Tax Credit Qualified Allocation Plan for public comment. A hybrid public hearing is set for June 8, 2026, and written comments are due by 5:00 P.M. on June 15, 2026.
